Lemma
[codimension-two zero-set classification]

Source: petersen:page-0340, petersen:page-0341 ↗ lem:pet-ch8-wilking-connectedness-principle ↗ def:pet-ch8-euler-characteristic 1. ch8:8.3.7Let $M$ be a closed $n$-manifold with positive sectional curvature. If $M$ admits a Killing field whose zero set has a component $N$ of codimension $2$, then $M$ is diffeomorphic to $S^n$, $\mathbb {CP}^{n/2}$, or a cyclic quotient of a sphere $S^n/\mathbb {Z}_q$.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch8-grove-searle-codim2 \sketch With codimension $2$, section 3 makes $N\hookrightarrow M$ $(n-2)$-connected. For simply connected $M$, the induced homology isomorphisms and Poincaré duality give two-periodicity:

\[ H_{j+2}(M)\simeq H_j(M),\qquad H^{j+2}(M)\simeq H^j(M) \]

in the interior range. Odd $n$ therefore gives the homology of a sphere; even $n$ gives the cohomology of either a sphere or $\mathbb {CP}^{n/2}$. The fixed-point tubular-neighborhood argument upgrades these alternatives to the asserted diffeomorphism types. On the universal cover the same analysis applies, and the deck group is cyclic, yielding the spherical quotients.

□
